feedbackActionPlan.summary: Rename the customer-facing vault plate color option to clarify that it refers to the ferrule-equivalent part under the tip, while keeping the shop term "vault plate" visible for internal consistency and experienced buyers.
feedbackActionPlan.customerImpact: Customers who do not know cue-building terminology can understand which visible cue part they are choosing before placing an order, reducing hesitation, support questions, and incorrect selections.
feedbackActionPlan.businessImpact: Small copy and label changes can reduce repetitive pre-sale questions, improve configurator completion confidence, and preserve precise shop language without retraining staff or changing product data.
feedbackActionPlan.confidence: High confidence because the raw feedback identifies repeated customer confusion, repository search did not expose a website implementation surface in this checkout, and external cue terminology research supports explaining vault plate as a ferrule-equivalent front-end part. Confidence is not 1.00 because the exact current UI component and available help-text patterns were not present in this repository.

researchFindings.finding: Raw feedback says customers frequently ask what the vault plate is and suggests including "vault plate/ferrule" or similar in the option label.

Repository inspection found feedback files but no website source paths such as app, pages, components, lib, or public; assumption: this checkout does not contain the live website/configurator implementation.
Pool cue ferrule terminology commonly describes the ferrule as the short front-end piece between the cue tip and shaft that supports or protects the shaft end.
Predator support describes the REVO Vault Plate as the equivalent of a wood-shaft ferrule, attached between the carbon tube and cue tip, but not identical to a conventional removable ferrule.

Predator product specifications use hybrid labeling such as "Vault Plate / Ferrule Color," which supports a customer-facing slash label that preserves the shop term while adding the more widely recognized ferrule term.

implementationPlan.step: Locate the order form or cue configurator field currently labeled "Vault Plate Color" and any related review, cart, email, invoice, or admin summary labels that repeat the selected option.
Change the primary customer-facing label to "Vault Plate / Ferrule Color" so the existing shop term remains first and searchable while the familiar cue-part term appears beside it.

Add concise help text directly under the field or in the existing tooltip pattern: "The small piece directly under the tip. On carbon-style shafts we call this the vault plate; on traditional shafts many players know it as the ferrule."
If space is constrained in summaries, use "Vault Plate / Ferrule" as the displayed option name and keep the selected color unchanged.
Keep internal data keys, SKU mappings, and shop/admin terminology unchanged unless the current system already separates display labels from internal identifiers.
Review nearby terminology for consistency so related options such as tip, shaft, collar, and joint still read as cue-part labels rather than mixed marketing copy.
Have a non-expert reviewer identify the part from the label and help text without staff explanation; adjust only if they still cannot tell that it is the front-end piece under the tip.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: The configurator/order form no longer shows the ambiguous standalone label "Vault Plate Color" to customers.
The customer-facing label includes both terms in this order: "Vault Plate / Ferrule Color".
Help text explains the location of the part as directly under the tip and clarifies the terminology difference between vault plate and ferrule.
Order summaries, confirmations, and staff-facing fulfillment views remain understandable and do not rename internal product identifiers unexpectedly.
No pricing, option availability, or selected color behavior changes as part of this copy update.

risks.risk: Using only "ferrule" could blur the technical distinction for carbon-style shafts and conflict with shop language.
Using only "vault plate" preserves precision but does not solve the customer comprehension problem described in the feedback.
Adding too much technical explanation beside the option could clutter the form; keep the visible help text short and defer deeper details to an optional tooltip or FAQ if needed.

openQuestions.question: Does the live website already have a reusable tooltip/help-text component for product-option fields?
Are vault plate color choices available only for carbon-style shafts, or does the same UI field also apply to traditional ferrules?
Should staff-facing paperwork keep "vault plate" only, or should it mirror the customer label for support consistency?
